reference_memory.normal_pattern: The channel exhibits a robust quasi-periodic oscillation with a fundamental period of ~95 points (1 cycle per 95 points), confirmed across all candidates. Each cycle contains a characteristic asymmetric waveform: a relatively sharp, narrow trough (~10–15 points wide) followed by a broader, smoother rising limb (~30–40 points) and a gentle decay to the next trough. Amplitude (90th percentile range) is stable at ~1.8–2.0 in robust standardized units, with median levels drifting slowly downward over long horizons (global trend slope ≈ −0.0002 per point). Noise is low-to-moderate: roughness (mean absolute first difference) ranges 0.039–0.057, curvature (second difference) 0.024–0.072, indicating mostly smooth transitions except near troughs where sharper drops occur. Peaks are rounded and rarely exceed +1.4; troughs are sharper and can dip below −1.5, especially in later segments. Boundary truncation is minimal—each candidate starts/ends mid-cycle, preserving full waveform morphology. The consensus normal pattern is stable across cycles, with minor inter-cycle amplitude modulation and consistent trough timing relative to cycle phase. Acceptable variation includes slight baseline shifts (±0.3), modest changes in trough depth (−1.2 to −1.6), and occasional minor overshoots on rises; deviations such as flatlined segments, abrupt sustained offsets (>0.5), or distorted cycle symmetry (e.g., inverted or double-peaked cycles) are outside normal bounds.

reference_profiles.description: Single-cycle (95-point) excerpt showing one full quasi-periodic wave: starts near +1.3, dips sharply to ~+0.65 at index ~5, then rises smoothly to ~+1.4 by index ~20, decays gently, and ends near +1.2. Low roughness (0.039), very mild negative slope (−0.0018/pt), clean morphology with no flat segments or outliers. Visually the most ‘textbook’ cycle.

Three-cycle (285-point) segment with clear periodicity; shows gradual baseline descent from +0.8 to −0.2 over the window. Troughs deepen slightly over time (from ~−0.2 to −0.6), peaks remain near +0.9–1.0. Contains a brief flat segment near index 1054 (value −0.5 for ~20 pts), which is atypical but isolated and not disruptive to overall rhythm. Moderate roughness (0.044) and curvature (0.039).

Three-cycle segment starting lower (median −0.16), with similar waveform shape but slightly deeper troughs (down to −1.3) and more pronounced rise limbs. Baseline drift is flatter than candidate 1 (slope +0.0002/pt). No flat segments; noise slightly higher (roughness 0.048, curvature 0.041). Morphology aligns closely with candidate 1, confirming core pattern robustness despite lower level.

Five-cycle (475-point) excerpt showing strongest long-term trend (slope −0.00043/pt), descending from ~−0.5 to −1.1. Amplitude compresses slightly (amplitude_90 = 1.79), troughs become shallower in later cycles. One notable artifact: a brief spike near index 2669 (−1.8 → −1.2 in 2 pts) followed by recovery—likely sensor glitch, but isolated. Overall morphology remains faithful to the consensus pattern across all five cycles.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 0 for queries with single-cycle length or high signal clarity; use reference 2 when query baseline is negative and troughs are deeper; reference 1 is suitable for moderate-drift, medium-length queries but disregard its flat segment as non-representative; reference 3 should only be used for long windows (>400 pts) where trend dominates—ignore its isolated spike. When comparing query morphology, match cycle-phase alignment (trough position relative to window start) rather than absolute y-level.
uncertainties: Exact trough width distribution (10–20 pts) varies slightly; whether this reflects true process variability or measurement noise is unresolved.
The isolated flat segment in ref 1 and spike in ref 3 could indicate rare transient faults; their frequency in the full train set is unknown.
Whether the mild cubic trend component manifests as subtle waveform warping over >5 cycles remains unverified due to limited long-window examples.
